headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading errors: TREK’s collaborative, secret-bearing workspace can ingest Pipecat outputs by default, while Pipecat can stream sensitive conversation content to external APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat exposes text/conversation state and shared-bus concurrency, while TREK is real-time collaborative with MCP and browser surfaces. That creates a plausible path for TREK content to be fed into Pipecat or vice versa as trusted instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so injection risk is real but not clearly default-high.
conditions: IF TREK content is routed into Pipecat prompts or memory without provenance tags
IF either agent parses the other’s text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add explicit provenance labels to all cross-agent messages
Strip executable markup from shared text before prompting
Require human review for any instruction-like content
Disable MCP routes that forward untrusted text
requires-engineering: add allowlist-based prompt schemas

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Pipecat sends text/audio/video through allowlisted network egress to multiple third-party APIs. If TREK shares workspace data with Pipecat, sensitive travel and credential data can leave the host through Pipecat’s inference calls. This is a default-dangerous exfiltration pathway.
conditions: IF TREK passes documents, photos, or secrets into Pipecat inputs
IF Pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS provider from its documented API list
mitigations: Keep secrets and documents out of Pipecat inputs
Route only redacted text to Pipecat
Disable external providers for sensitive sessions
Separate TREK and Pipecat workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat supports shared-bus state across multiple instances, and TREK is real-time collaborative with files and databases. Both can mutate shared session state, so overlapping writes can race or overwrite each other if orchestrated together. The profiles do not prove same-directory writes, so this is a conflict risk but not the highest tier.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared session or file-backed state
IF no external locking or transaction boundary is present
mitigations: Assign separate state stores per agent
Use a lock around shared writes
Serialize updates through one coordinator
Turn off multi-instance sharing for the shared resource
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is collaborative and AI-assisted, so it can plausibly consume Pipecat-generated text as authoritative travel advice or actions. Pipecat can emit conversational content from audio/video inputs, and TREK manages reservations and budgets; a bad Pipecat output could cascade into incorrect bookings or user-facing plans. No verification step is documented, so the default path is dangerous.
conditions: IF TREK uses Pipecat output as a source for itinerary, reservation, or budget actions
IF TREK lacks a verification step before rendering or acting on Pipecat output
mitigations: Require confirmation before any booking or edit
Show Pipecat output as untrusted draft text
Add source citations to all generated claims
Block direct action execution from model output
requires-engineering: add validation against authoritative APIs

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and user accounts, while Pipecat processes audio/video/text and can send data to external providers. If regulated or sensitive travel data is routed into Pipecat, retention and residency obligations may diverge from TREK’s local self-hosted storage model. The profiles do not show a specific legal regime, so this is a compliance-mismatch risk, not critical.
conditions: IF regulated personal data from TREK is forwarded to Pipecat providers
IF retention or deletion policies differ between TREK storage and Pipecat vendors
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Pipecat sessions
Document a shared retention policy
Purge logs after sensitive sessions
Use self-hosted providers where possible
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency requirements
